talks.title: Come to the Lord in His Holy House
talks.speaker: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
talks.summary: Elder Gong invites each family to build its own temple culture on three doctrines: the Father's work of bringing families home through covenants, the Savior's power to change and heal us, including strained family relationships, and the Holy Spirit of Promise sealing what we faithfully keep. He asks members to worship in the temple often, value every temple regardless of size, consider owning temple clothing, and take relatives' names. Discussion could explore what temple worship looks like in our homes.
talks.seed: What has temple service for a relative changed in how you feel about your own family?

talks.title: The Sculpting of Our Souls
talks.speaker: Sister Tamara W. Runia
talks.calling: First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
talks.summary: Speaking from the sudden death of her adult son, Sister Runia teaches that God shapes our souls through hardship rather than sparing us from it, and that the gospel gives footing in the storm rather than shelter from the rain. She asks listeners to move from asking why trials come to asking what God is forming in them, to stop comparing their story with others', and to let the Savior do the shaping. Expect a tender discussion of grief and trust.
talks.seed: Looking back on a hard season, what do you see now that God was shaping in you?

talks.title: The Gift of Testimony
talks.speaker: Elder Gérald Caussé
talks.summary: Elder Caussé teaches that a testimony of Jesus Christ is a gift of the Spirit meant to be shared, and that the Holy Ghost can carry even a short, plain witness into another heart. Bearing it also strengthens the one who shares it. He invites every disciple to watch each day for chances to testify: at home, while ministering, online, and in ordinary conversation. Discussion could explore what makes testifying feel hard, and what makes it natural.
talks.seed: When has someone's simple testimony stayed with you?

talks.title: Prophets, Seers, and Revelators
talks.speaker: Elder Vaiangina Sikahema
talks.summary: Elder Sikahema warns against treating the words of living prophets lightly, and contrasts that casualness with his Tongan grandparents, who in 1947 sailed through a storm to meet an Apostle and be sealed, burying their infant son on the way. He asks us to value the rare blessing of living prophets and heed them, beginning with this conference. Discussion could weigh what receiving prophetic counsel costs us now, and what it once cost others.
talks.seed: What counsel from a living prophet has made a practical difference in your life?

talks.title: Jesus Christ Is the Great Deliverer!
talks.speaker: Elder Kevin J. Hathaway
talks.summary: Elder Hathaway traces a pattern in scripture: affliction raises hard questions, people seek the Lord, He assures those who keep their covenants, His grace helps them endure, and deliverance comes in His time, whether as a miracle now, relief later, or the Resurrection. He draws on a highway accident his family survived and a missionary whose father died just before she came home. He invites us to turn to Christ and hold fast to our covenants.
talks.seed: Where have you seen deliverance come later, or differently, than you first hoped?

talks.title: A Higher and Holier Fast
talks.speaker: Elder Ulisses Soares
talks.summary: Working mainly from Isaiah 58, Elder Soares teaches that fasting joined with prayer is an act of worship, not simply going without food. It aligns our will with God's, opens the way to inspiration, and turns outward through generous fast offerings for people in need. He invites members to study Isaiah's chapter on the fast and to fast more deliberately, while recognizing that some cannot for health reasons. It fits naturally near a fast Sunday.
talks.seed: What has made a fast feel like worship to you, rather than just hunger?

talks.title: The Hour of Your Mission Is Come
talks.speaker: Bishop Sean Douglas
talks.calling: Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
talks.summary: Bishop Douglas speaks to the rising generation, teaching that they were prepared for this moment in the gathering of Israel and that missionaries are sent by the Savior Himself. He asks young men to see a mission as a priesthood duty, young women to pray about serving, and recent converts to consider it too. In quorum, discussion could focus on how we prepare and support the youth around us.
talks.seed: What did someone do that helped you, or a young person you love, decide to serve a mission?

talks.title: O Be Wise
talks.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
talks.calling: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
talks.summary: President Christofferson addresses gambling directly, including the sports-betting apps, online casino games, and prediction markets that now live on every phone. He teaches that gambling means taking without giving value, often at another person's expense, and so conflicts with loving our neighbor; it also spends time and money that could do good. He asks members to avoid it entirely and to weigh their example to youth and others easily drawn in. Discussion could turn practical, especially for parents.
talks.seed: How do we help our families think through choices the culture around us treats as harmless?

talks.title: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
talks.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
talks.summary: Elder Renlund teaches that we can have joy and peace through Christ now, yet we tend to fix on present troubles and forget God's past mercies. He recalls a heart-transplant patient whose first complaint after recovering was cold oatmeal, and his sister's private belief that God's promises applied to everyone but her. He invites us to record God's hand daily and to trust His promises rather than our own adequacy. A natural fit for Thanksgiving week.
talks.seed: What blessing have you nearly overlooked because a small annoyance was louder?

talks.title: Divine Appointments
talks.speaker: President Timothy L. Farnes
talks.summary: President Farnes teaches that taking Christ's name in the sacrament includes promising to see people as He sees them, and that ordinary encounters can be appointments God has arranged. He tells of nearly skipping a ward temple night and being encouraged there by Elder Oaks, who later didn't remember it, and of helping a frightened new missionary at an airport. He invites us to pray daily to notice these moments and to act with compassion rather than judgment.
talks.seed: When has an interruption turned out to be exactly where the Lord needed you?

talks.title: Spiritual Immunity
talks.speaker: Elder Christian C. Chigbundu
talks.summary: Elder Chigbundu borrows an idea from pandemic health briefings: as the body builds immunity, the soul can build protection against trials and temptation. He names four habits that build it: scripture study, especially the Book of Mormon; prayer in faith; taking the sacrament worthily; and keeping covenants, including temple worship. He tells of a homesick missionary who found purpose through daily study and a sister with cancer sustained by prayer. Discussion could get practical about keeping small habits steady.
talks.seed: Which small daily habit has protected you most when life got hard?

talks.title: Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings
talks.speaker: Elder Patricio M. Giuffra
talks.summary: Elder Giuffra teaches that tithing is a law of faith that applies to everyone, whatever their income, and that keeping it can help families break cycles of poverty. As a young missionary in Chile, he taught an elderly widow who felt she could not afford to pay; after learning of the widow's mite, she prayed, was baptized, and paid faithfully. He invites us to obey out of love rather than to earn blessings, and to be patient with the Lord's timing.
talks.seed: When has obeying a commandment required trust before you could see the blessing?

talks.title: The Infinite Power of God in Our Covenants
talks.speaker: Elder Jeremiah J. Morgan
talks.summary: Elder Morgan, raised in the Community of Christ, traces his own conversion to covenants his third-great-grandparents made in Nauvoo, and teaches that God's covenant promises reach children and grandchildren across generations without overriding their agency. Enos's prayer for his people, still being answered, shows that those promises do not expire. He invites parents of children who have strayed not to despair, to keep their own covenants, and to keep reading the Book of Mormon.
talks.seed: How has a covenant someone made before you shaped your own life?

talks.title: I Am a Child of God
talks.speaker: Elder Hutch U. Fale
talks.summary: Elder Fale teaches that every person is a child of Heavenly Father with a divine nature, and that His love is never earned and so can never be lost, though His full blessings come through covenants. He makes the point with his children's baby pictures, and recalls feeling God's love reading John 3:16 as a boy in Tonga. Knowing who we are, he says, guards against worldly labels and against believing we cannot change. He invites us to turn to Christ now.
talks.seed: How does remembering that someone is a child of God change the way you treat them?

talks.title: Jesus Lives to Lift
talks.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
talks.summary: Elder Kearon, who learned to fly gliders as a teenager in England, compares spiritual life to soaring on rising air: the Savior lifts those who turn to Him, often through quiet promptings we learn to feel, while neglect brings a slow, unnoticed descent, and no one holds altitude for long. He invites us to notice our own moments of lift and sinking, stay close to people who are climbing, turn from early signs of decline, and help others find lift.
talks.seed: What helps you notice early that you're drifting downward spiritually, and what lifts you again?

talks.title: The Ninety and Ten
talks.speaker: Elder Michael A. Dunn
talks.summary: Elder Dunn tells of running his first 100-mile race and quitting at mile 90, until a friend talked him back onto the trail; a photo later showed that the friend had quietly carried his water for the last ten miles. He teaches that the Savior usually strengthens us to finish rather than shortening the road, and often carries our burdens in ways we recognize only afterward. He invites the weary to ask for help and to trust Him completely.
talks.seed: Looking back, when did you realize the Lord had been carrying more of the load than you knew?

talks.title: Comfort from the Holy Ghost
talks.speaker: Elder Matthew J. Eyring
talks.summary: Elder Eyring teaches that self-reliance has limits: everyone eventually meets a loss they cannot fix. The Savior's Atonement rescues us from permanent loss, and along the way He sends the Holy Ghost to comfort us now. He tells of a friend whose son died suddenly and a young couple who lost a twin before birth, a loss he and his wife also knew. He invites us to give the Lord our burdens and to make the Spirit's companionship a priority.
talks.seed: How has the Holy Ghost comforted you, or someone you served, in a loss you couldn't fix?

talks.title: Love Like Jesus
talks.speaker: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
talks.summary: Elder Rasband speaks to parents and family members grieving over loved ones who have left the faith. He teaches that only the Savior can change a heart, that each person chooses for themselves, and that our part is to love as Christ does and keep praying, as Alma's father did for years. His counsel is practical: stay present, put the person ahead of the problem, release self-blame, and never give up. Plan the discussion with care.
talks.seed: What has helped you keep loving someone whose choices break your heart?

tags.audience: Families of loved ones who have left the faith

talks.title: “Fear Not, I Am with Thee”
talks.speaker: President Henry B. Eyring
talks.calling: First Counselor in the First Presidency
talks.summary: President Eyring teaches that hardship is a purposeful part of mortal life, and that the Savior's promised comfort comes both directly through the Spirit and through disciples who act as His hands. He remembers his mother's lifelong health struggles, the picture of the Savior she kept in view during her last illness, and his father thanking each nurse who cared for her. He invites us to pray for family, friends, missionaries, and leaders, and to act on promptings to comfort.
talks.seed: When were you the answer to someone's prayer, or they the answer to yours?

talks.title: A Child of God
talks.speaker: President Rosemary K. Chibota
talks.summary: President Chibota builds on a southern African greeting that means "I see you," teaching that disciples learn to see people as the Savior does: as children of God rather than by worldly labels. She points to Jesus noticing the man at Bethesda whom others had passed for 38 years; she offers three weekly practices: learn the name of someone who feels unseen, pray to see others as God does, and use eternal labels.
talks.seed: Who in our ward or neighborhood might feel unseen, and how could we notice them this week?

talks.title: Courage Born of Our Faith in Jesus Christ
talks.speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
talks.summary: Elder Andersen teaches that faith in Christ and spiritual courage strengthen each other: faith gives courage to choose rightly, and courageous choices deepen faith. Today's distractions and misinformation make that courage necessary. His examples range from President Chibota's teenage conversion in Zimbabwe and Moroni standing alone to a family who kept their faith after wildfire took their home. He invites quiet, device-free time with God, serious attention to the sacrament, and accepting callings that feel too large.
talks.seed: When did acting on your faith take courage, and what did it teach you?

talks.title: Take Upon Us His Name
talks.speaker: Elder James G. O. Fantone
talks.summary: Elder Fantone teaches that taking Christ's name upon us is more than claiming a religious identity: it is a covenant to serve Him by serving others, a lifelong commitment that changes the heart. He contrasts it with the time he wrote his own name on his daughter's school form by mistake, and remembers his parents opening their small home to people who needed shelter. He invites us to lose ourselves in lifting others, as homesick missionaries find joy once they forget themselves.
talks.seed: What does carrying the Savior's name look like on an ordinary Tuesday?

talks.title: Come unto Christ
talks.speaker: Elder Edward Dube
talks.calling: Of the Presidency of the Seventy
talks.summary: Drawing on Moroni's final invitation, Elder Dube teaches that we do not have to be perfect before coming to Christ; we come so that He can perfect us through His grace. He tells of a man struggling to quit smoking who simply did his best; he and his wife were sealed two months later. He invites anyone weighed down by addiction, doubt, guilt, or grief to come as they are, and each of us to invite one person to Christ.
talks.seed: What helped you, or someone you love, stop waiting to be “good enough” before coming to Christ?

talks.title: Integrity and Virtue Lead to Happiness
talks.speaker: Elder Quentin L. Cook
talks.summary: Elder Cook teaches that integrity, virtue, and happiness belong together in God's plan, defining virtue broadly as moral character, goodness, modesty, and reverence for sacred things. He applies this to the coarse tone of online life and asks members to be peacemakers there. He recalls a World War II veteran he taught as a young missionary, for whom forgiveness felt like coming home from war. He invites daily scripture study, daily repentance, and service as the path to lasting joy.
talks.seed: Where is it hardest to keep the same character online that you keep in person?

talks.title: Using the Language of Peacemakers
talks.speaker: Elder Alfred Kyungu
talks.summary: Elder Kyungu treats everyday speech as part of discipleship: words can wound or build, and choosing peaceful, respectful language takes deliberate work. Like the converted Lamanites who buried their weapons, he asks us to identify and bury our own hurtful phrases, repent of harsh words, and pray to speak peacefully when we disagree. He offers side-by-side examples of dismissive and caring expressions for home, work, and church. Discussion could lead to honest self-examination.
talks.seed: Which phrase would you like to retire from how you speak at home?

talks.title: “Consider Your Ways, and from This Day Will the Lord Bless You”
talks.speaker: Elder Ciro Schmeil
talks.summary: Elder Schmeil builds on the prophet Haggai, who told Israel they were tending their own houses while the Lord's house lay unfinished, and promised blessing from the day they turned back. Mortality, he teaches, is the time to prepare to meet God, and the Father has given two helps for the journey: Jesus Christ and covenants, renewed each week through the sacrament. He invites us to look honestly at our priorities and to come to the sacrament willing, not perfect.
talks.seed: If you “considered your ways” this week, what one priority would you change?

talks.title: The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All
talks.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
talks.calling: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
talks.summary: President Oaks teaches that the restored gospel and the Savior's Atonement are offered to every person, whatever their race, standing, or sex, on the same conditions of faith, repentance, and baptism. He speaks directly to members whose faith is weakening, counseling daily prayer and scripture study, patience, covenant keeping, and a teachable heart, and reminding them that spiritual truth comes by revelation as well as study. He also points to scripture yet to come from scattered Israel.
talks.seed: What has helped you hold on when questions made faith feel harder?

talks.title: Christ-Centered Unity
talks.speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
talks.calling: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
talks.summary: President Uchtdorf teaches that the Church's unity rests on Jesus Christ, not on shared politics, culture, or interests. The adversary isolates us by magnifying differences; as each of us draws nearer to the Savior, we draw nearer to one another. He recalls his own baptism at eight in a public pool, and the Nephites and Lamanites who lived as one people for two centuries after Christ came. He closes with a threefold invitation: come and see, come and help, come and belong.
talks.seed: What helps you feel united with someone whose views differ sharply from yours?

talks.title: God Is at Your Side
talks.speaker: Sister Andrea Muñoz Spannaus
talks.calling: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
talks.summary: Speaking mainly to young women, Sister Spannaus teaches that Heavenly Father knows exactly where each of them is, as her husband guided her home once he learned where she really was after her phone's map misled her. Drawing on the thirteenth article of faith, she invites them to write down worthy goals and choose one of seven habits to work on, from protecting sleep and limiting phone use to daily repentance and choosing good friends. Useful for fathers of daughters.
talks.seed: Which of her seven habits would make the biggest difference in your home right now?

talks.title: “Prove Me Now Herewith”
talks.speaker: Elder Moisés Villanueva
talks.summary: Elder Villanueva teaches that the Lord's blessings for paying tithing often come quietly, in ways we may miss if we are watching for a raise or a promotion. He recalls his mother raising eight children alone while paying tithing, a sister whose propane tank lasted far longer than it should have, the widow of Zarephath's flour and oil, and Israel's clothing that did not wear out in forty years. He invites us to write our own list of quiet tithing blessings.
talks.seed: What quiet blessing from paying tithing have you recognized only in hindsight?

talks.title: Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise
talks.speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
talks.summary: Elder Bednar teaches that ordinances are credentials for returning to God, but they must be kept with integrity, as a traveler learns when a border officer refuses his battered passport. The Holy Spirit of Promise confirms our covenants, usually gradually, through steady repentance and faithfulness. He states plainly that a faithful spouse cannot lose sealing blessings because of a partner's broken covenants or a divorce, and explains why. The discussion may touch members in hard marriages; plan it with care.
talks.seed: What helps you keep your covenants current rather than letting them sit untouched?

talks.title: Jesus Christ Is the Light and Life of the World
talks.speaker: Elder Thabo Lebethoa
talks.summary: Elder Lebethoa teaches that whatever we face, the answer is Jesus Christ, whose light reaches us through His Spirit, His example, and His words. He tells of an early argument with his wife that ended when he remembered the Savior's teaching against contention. He names three daily practices that let that light grow: building faith in Christ; studying scripture, especially the Book of Mormon, in whatever way works for you; and repenting daily. Short and practical, it suits a first Sunday.
talks.seed: What daily habit most reliably lets the Savior's light into your home?

talks.title: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
talks.speaker: Elder Paul H. Sinclair
talks.summary: Elder Sinclair begins with a Primary program in which a boy buttoned his sleeve to his lapel; he felt irritated, but the girl beside the boy simply unbuttoned it. From that small rebuke he turns to the Savior at the well, who gave the Samaritan woman dignity and truth and saw who she could become rather than her past. He invites us to help rather than judge, especially with new members and friends being taught.
talks.seed: What made you feel at home when you were new to a ward?

talks.title: Fruit to Make One Happy
talks.speaker: Elder Gary E. Stevenson
talks.summary: Speaking largely to Primary children, Elder Stevenson uses the fruit in Lehi's vision to teach that gospel truths, like fresh fruit, are known by tasting them, by living them. He names three favorites: that we are children of a loving Heavenly Father, the plan of happiness centered in the Savior's Atonement, and the gift of the Holy Ghost. Stories include a boy singing beside him after an earthquake and a grieving Buddhist priest in Japan finding peace.
talks.seed: Which gospel truth did you first “taste” by living it rather than hearing it?

talks.title: You Are Good Enough to Teach
talks.speaker: Brother Gabriel W. Reid
talks.calling: Second Counselor in the Sunday School General Presidency
talks.summary: Brother Reid, who grew up one of thirteen children in American Samoa and later played in the NFL, teaches that love for the Savior and for learners, not polish or expertise, is what qualifies a gospel teacher. He speaks directly to the new 25-minute lessons, inviting teachers to measure success by whether people leave closer to Christ. It suits the start of the season, or a word to instructors.
talks.seed: Who taught you the gospel in a way you still remember, and what made it work?

talks.title: Teach Truth with Love
talks.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
talks.summary: Elder Gilbert teaches that disciples must hold firmly to truth and show real love at the same time, letting neither crowd out the other. Building on five principles from President Oaks, he counsels checking our own pride first, avoiding heated settings, listening for common ground, and never setting aside commandments in love's name. He candidly tells of winning an argument with a former friend while losing the Spirit, and of a ministering visit where patient listening opened five hearts.
talks.seed: When have you seen someone stand for truth and still leave the other person feeling loved?

talks.title: Closing Remarks
talks.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
talks.calling: President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
talks.summary: In brief closing remarks, President Oaks reminds members that conference centered their worship on Jesus Christ and the Father's plan, and promises that those who study and act on its messages will be given more. He announces that the Salt Lake Temple will open to the public on April 5, 2027, for the first time since 1893, and introduces a new video series, Dedicate. At only a few minutes, it works best paired with another talk or on a counsel Sunday.
talks.seed: What will help us actually study these conference messages, rather than only hear them?
